beliefs: For strings of length 1, the single character is lowercased and '10' is prepended [E2, E4, E8]
For strings of length >=2, the first character is titlecased (str.title(), which may expand to multiple chars like 'ß'->'Ss', 'ﬁ'->'Fi', 'ǆ'->'ǅ') [E1, E2, E4, E9]
All characters after the first are lowercased [E1, E2, E3]
The '10' is inserted at index floor(len/2) of the original string length, computed on the lowercased-rest string BEFORE titlecasing the first char [E2, E4, E5, E6, E7, E9]
Order of operations: lowercase rest, insert '10' at floor(len/2), then titlecase the first character (which may grow the string) [E9]
For 'ßabc' -> 'Ssa10bc': '10' goes at index 2 (floor(4/2)), then 'ß'->'Ss' expands [E9]
notes: E9 revealed the first char is titlecased (not uppercased) and that '10' insertion uses the original length on the pre-titlecase string, then the first char is titlecased last (allowing length expansion).
